stem:
Consider the following statements regarding Wood’s Dispatch of 1854 :
1. It recommended English as the medium of instruction for higher studies.
2. It laid stress on female education and vocational training.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
expl: In 1854, the Court of Directors of the East India Company in London sent a note to the Governor-General of India, Lord Dalhousie, on the subject of education. In response, Charles Wood, the President of the Board of Control, issued a policy document in July 1854, which is known as ‘Wood’s Despatch’ or ‘Wood’s policy document/charter’. This charter prepared a comprehensive plan for future education in India, and it is called the ‘Magna Carta’ of English education in India. Wood’s Despatch made the following recommendations— (i) Emphasis was laid on imparting higher education through the medium of the English language; however, importance was also given to the development of vernacular (native) languages. (ii) It recommended women’s education and vocational training. (iv) Establishment of one university each in the three Presidencies (Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras) on the model of the University of London. (v) Establishment of teacher training institutions for the training of teachers. Therefore, the required answer will be option (c).

stem: When did Macaulay issue his famous minute on Indian Education?
expl: To resolve the Orientalist–Western controversy over the medium of education in India, William Bentinck appointed Macaulay (a law member in his Council) in 1834 as the head of the General Committee of Public Instruction. His task was to present a decision on the language dispute. Macaulay submitted his memorandum/minute on 2 February 1835, in which he sharply criticized Indian languages and literature. Accepting the main recommendations of Macaulay’s Minute, Governor-General Bentinck issued a resolution on 7 March 1835, making English the medium of higher education in India.

stem: Who said, "A single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia"?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The foundation of the modern education system in India was laid by Macaulay’s Minute (1835). Macaulay believed that “a single shelf in a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia.” Ignoring Indian culture, he described it as a “storehouse of superstitions.” He wanted to spread Western education among Indians and create a group that would be Indian in colour and blood, but English in thought, taste, and intellect.

stem: To what was Wood's Dispatch of 1854 related?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Wood’s Despatch (1854) is called the “Magna Carta of Indian Education.” It emphasized modern education. It made provision for establishing universities in the three Presidency towns—Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras—on the pattern of the University of London. It also recommended setting up a Department of Public Instruction in each province. Therefore, option (d) is correct.

expl: Banaras Hindu University was established in 1916 by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya. It was established under a legislative enactment, the B.H.U. Act, 1915.

stem: ________ passed the Indian Universities Act in 1904, implementing strict controls on Indian universities.
expl: Lord Curzon was the Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905. During his tenure, to carry out educational reforms, he constituted a “University Commission” in 1902 under the chairmanship of Sir Thomas Raleigh. Based on the commission’s recommendations, the Indian Universities Act was passed in 1904. Under this Act, government control over universities increased.

expl: Fort William College in Calcutta was established by the then Governor-General Wellesley of the East India Company. The college was formally established on 4 May 1800, and the legal and administrative regulations related to its formation were approved on 10 July 1800. The main objective of this college was to train British civil servants in Persian and Indian languages for administration in India.

stem: When was the National Council of Education established?
expl: In the field of national education, the “Rangpur National School” was established on 8 November 1905. A conference was held in Calcutta on 16 November 1905. In this conference, it was decided to establish the “National Council of Education” to provide national literary, scientific, and technical education. On the basis of official records and authentic historical documents, the correct date of establishment of the National Council of Education is 11 March 1906, not 15 August 1906. On 11 March 1906, the National Council of Education was constituted through a resolution passed during a public conference in Kolkata. It is considered the first concrete step of the Swadeshi education campaign of the Indian freedom movement. The date given in the options—15 August 1906—was the day when the first National College (Bengal National School), under the aegis of the National Council of Education, was started.

stem: Which of the following was not an objective of the Indian National Congress as pointed out by W.C. Banerjee in 1885?

options.label: a
options.text: To promote contact and friendship among the protectors of the interests of the country.

options.label: b
options.text: To promote the feeling of nationalism among fellow countrymen by removing the feeling of casteism, communalism and regional biases.

options.label: c
options.text: To express the viewpoint on the necessary social issues with due consent of the educated class.

options.label: d
options.text: To determine on which direction and on which basis the work has to be done in the coming years for the Indian public interest.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In 1885, at the first session of the Indian National Congress, the following objectives were stated as indicated by Womesh Chandra Banerjee— (1) To Promote contact and friendship among the protectors of the interests of the country; (2) To Promote feelings of nationalism among fellow countrymen by removing the feeling of casteism, communalism and regional biases. (3) To express the viewpoint on the necessary social issues with due consent of the educated class. (4) To determine on which direction and on which basis to work has to be done in the coming years for the Indian public interest. It is noteworthy that, in the beginning, there was a provision/ arrangement that social issues would not be taken up from the Congress platform.

stem: When did the British Government appoint the Sadler University Commission for reforms in education :
expl: The Sadler Commission (Calcutta University Commission) was related to education. In 1917, the Government of India appointed a commission to study the condition and prospects of the University of Calcutta and to submit its report. Dr. M. E. Sadler, who was the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Leeds, was appointed as its Chairman. The Commission held that if university education was to be improved, reform of secondary education was essential. It strongly criticized the University Act of 1904 and stated that, because of it, proper coordination between college education and university education was not possible.

stem: By whom was the Asiatic Society established in Calcutta?'
expl: The Asiatic Society in Calcutta was founded in 1784 by Sir William Jones. Through this institution, many important Indian texts were translated into English.
